title: Compliance Type is required free text and can be renamed
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in as an Owner/Admin, or a user with "Settings Service" enabled, on the build under test. The Maintenance Reminders feature is on (behind the maintenance_reminders flag).
  2. A schedule open in the editor with a service form ready. Seed it:
  3. ↳ Settings > Maintenance > New schedule (or open a schedule and Edit).
  4. ↳ Click Add service to open the service form.
  5. ↳ Turn on "Is this a compliance inspection?" so the compliance block shows.
  6. At least one compliance type already exists and is referenced by a record (so deletion can be tried).
custom_steps:
1. Read the Type field and open its (i) for examples; try to Save with Type blank.
  2. Rename an existing compliance type.
  3. Try to delete a type that a record still references.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Type is free text and required; an (i) beside it shows examples: Annual safety, Annual state, Annual federal, Emissions test.
  • A compliance type that has been added can be renamed, and cannot be deleted while any record still references it.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-3780; story SV-10560 (S3, Add a compliance inspection service); Chunk 1 MR spec (Confluence 886931488), S3; read 29 Sep 2026. Source-verified 29 September 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S3-R3: “Type is free text and required. An (i) beside it shows examples: Annual safety, Annual state, Annual federal, Emissions test”
  • S3-R12: “A compliance type a shop has added can be renamed, and cannot be deleted while any record still references it”
